div.div:
μὴ γάρ , an elliptic phrase, freq. in emphatic denial, or in assenting to a denial or prohibition, etc.,
A.certainly not, where Verb in imper. or opt. must be supplied from the context, μὴ λεγέτω τὸ ὄνομα . . Answ. μὴ γάρ [λεγέτω] Pl. Tht. 177e , cf. Sph. 255b : not in a reply, μὴ γὰρ δὴ δίναν γ᾽ Εὐρώτα (sc. ἔλθοιμι) E. Tr. 210 (lyr.): in parenthesis, where it may be translated much less (cf. μὴ ὅτι), Aeschin. 2.158 ; “μὴ γὰρ τῆς πόλεώς γε μηδ᾽ ἐμοῦ”
D. 18.200
.
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
